analysis:
The PR is documentation-only. It adds one table row to docs/architecture/inference.md at head line 1090 (prompt-chunk attention) and one env-var row to docs/reference/configuration.md at head line 397 (DARKBLOOM_TTFT_FUSED_CAUSAL_PREFILL). Together they describe a default-on fused causal SDPA path for eligible full-attention prefill chunks. The path excludes windowed, softcap, vision-span and bidirectional masks, and live packed paged KV. Setting the variable to exactly 0 restores 128-query blocks. The variable is read once per process and is not forwarded to LaunchAgents.

I found no change to authentication, attestation, encryption, cache scoping or the wire protocol. The prefix-cache SSD tier (T-041), its TTL, HMAC lookup tags and DBK3 AAD are untouched. Cache keys are not affected by the documented attention-kernel selection.

The prefill kernel change is a compute-path choice inside the provider process, so the TB-007 trust boundary and the decrypted-prompt-in-memory assumption are unchanged. The env knob is local operator-controlled configuration with the same standing as the other DARKBLOOM_CBV2_* knobs. Documentation of the knob adds no new attack surface. The operator is already the adversary for the provider process (TB-003), and nothing here weakens a control against that adversary.

The actual kernel change in AttentionV1.swift is not in the supplied evidence. Open questions: whether fused causal prefill preserves masking correctness, to avoid cross-request attention leaks in batched or paged contexts, and whether prefill memory admission accounts for any change in workspace. Both are outside this documentation diff and need review in the source PR. The patch excerpt for configuration.md was truncated, and head_text was not supplied for it. This does not affect the conclusion because the visible added row is complete.
